title: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
claim: Single-step policies forget task history; condensing multi-frame context into compact slots fixes this and beats the baselines across benchmarks.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: failure examples, method pipeline, bar-chart evaluation
description: A three-panel figure with a blue header on each panel. The left panel, 'History-dependent Tasks', shows two rows of robot camera frames for Pick and Place Twice and for Swap Cubes. Green, orange and red borders mark progress toward failure. Robot icons carry speech bubbles such as 'Wait, which plate for this next?'. The middle panel, 'CondenseVLA', is the pipeline. Multi-frame observations pass through a frozen VLM backbone to per-frame features in a history buffer. Learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention, with an attention matrix heatmap, produce condensed history. A diffusion action decoder with a feature modulator, cross-attention and iterative denoising outputs an action chunk. The right panel, 'Evaluation', has three bar charts for Simpler-WidowX, LIBERO and Real World. Ours is orange, and green arrows show gains over CronusVLA and OpenVLA-OFT.
caption: We propose \MethodName, a decoder-side \ModuleName\ (\ModuleShort) model that distills informative multi-frame context into compact slot tokens. The left panel highlights history-dependent failures of single-step VLA execution: in Pick and Place Twice, the policy forgets which plate to place next; in Swap Cubes, it forgets which cube should be picked next. Across multiple benchmarks, including Simpler, LIBERO, and real-world robot experiments, \MethodName\ consistently outperforms the CronusVLA baseline.
abstract: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window.
